question: Classify 66 bypass_attempt records and establish whether the sealed-pile guarantee holds on the arm that talks to the real API, not merely on the proxy side.

classification.note: buckets a and b are not disjoint here; that is the answer

ticket_premise_refuted: all 66 carry arm='probe', run_id='probe-model-proxy' and predate the arm (evidence/README.md:9-10); proxy/ledger.py:36-38 registers 'probe' as an identity distinct from 'theoria'. They are not on the real arm.
verdict_proxy_side: HOLDS -- every evasion attempted by the adversarial audit was refused with 403 before any socket opened
verdict_arm_side: DOES NOT HOLD YET -- (i) the arm process holds the live ARC credential (run.py:161 starts EnvProxy in-process; env_proxy.py:78 read_secret), (ii) the model path traverses no sealed-pile guard (modelcall.py:503-518), (iii) the model subprocess env scrub is config-bypassable (modelcall.py:505-508)
mechanism_finding: bypass_attempt logs and falls through; model_proxy.py:176-181 has no return. Enforcement is the PASSTHROUGH_REQUEST_HEADERS allowlist in _forward, a separate mechanism. The 66 401s came from upstream for want of an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not from the proxy refusing.
privacy_finding: theoria-arm/evidence/model-proxy-401.jsonl is tracked, 5.8 MB, and carries account_uuid/device_id/session_id 65 times each plus Claude Code's system prompt. No bearer tokens or oauth literals (0 each) -- operator identifiers, not credentials. Phase 4 publishes every tracked file.
method: one classifier subagent + one adversarial auditor tasked with finding a real bypass; every load-bearing claim re-read in the source by W-1641 before being written down
